name: Mandarin Corner
why: This handle is the Indonesian school mandarincorner.id (descriptions say 'Dibuat oleh: Syakcin', YouTube auto-captions are id-orig), not Eileen's channel that the classifier described from memory; its recent videos are 25-40 min New HSK 1 lessons explained in Indonesian with Mandarin example dialogues (4 of 9 clips Mandarin, the 'nospeech' clips are most likely Indonesian SenseVoice can't recognise). The audio label is right by luck: its 0.67 counted the Indonesian clips as silence.

name: 小凱BO-Kai (Follow me to veg out)
why: Only one of the three sampled videos (the 108 s corn video) has narration, in fluent Taiwanese Mandarin; the 676 s 快炒店 video and the third one are ambient vendor footage with a few words. The latest uploads are 61 s Shorts that weren't sampled, so it can't be told whether the channel's typical video is narrated Mandarin or mostly no speech; the audio's share=1 ignores that 6 of 9 clips had no speech.

name: Kiki 's Vlog  小日子
why: All 9 clips across the three latest 20-28 min Japan travel vlogs had no speech, matching the silent music-and-captions vlog style (Traditional Chinese subtitles only). A viewer hears almost no Mandarin, so 'other' fits better than 'unknown'.

name: MY FM 好玩
why: Astro's own brand page lists MY FM as 50% Mandarin / 50% Cantonese, and the clips split the same way (4 Malaysian Mandarin, 4 Cantonese, with code-switching inside clips). The classifier's 'mainly Mandarin' came from memory without a search.

name: 客家電視 HakkaTV
why: Hakka TV is the public Hakka-language broadcaster and its hosts, dramas and singing shows are in Hakka. SenseVoice has no Hakka, so Hakka came out as empty 'zh', 'yue' or garbled text; the only fluent Mandarin was three clips of one cafe-owner guest interview (EP72), which doesn't represent the channel.

name: Xiaomanyc 小马在纽约
why: Videos are narrated in English; about 5 of the latest 15 are Mandarin-themed (roughly 22% of upload time), and even those are partly English, so Mandarin is around 10-15% of what a viewer hears. The classifier's 30% leaned on his older China-heavy catalogue.

name: Mandarin Monkey
why: 8 of 9 clips from the three latest episodes are English, with Ula also speaking English and only scattered Mandarin words; the newest titles have dropped 'Mandarin & English podcast'. The classifier's 50% came from podcast directory blurbs describing the old format; episodes from a few months back (Ep. 472-483) may still be closer to 'mixed'.

name: Blondie in China
why: All 9 clips are English narration of China food videos, and the recent catalogue is entirely English-titled food travel. The Mandarin spoken with locals is brief; the classifier's 30% is an unsupported guess.

name: 讲闲话的夏安七
why: Every speech clip is fluent standard Mandarin commentary (Shanghai housing, city culture); only the 146 s '上海话的尽头' video had no recognisable speech. The classifier inferred heavy Shanghainese from the channel's dialect topics, but the narration itself is Mandarin.

name: MIRROR
why: The channel is official music videos for a Hong Kong Cantopop group, all with Cantonese titles. SenseVoice transcribed sung Cantonese as 'zh' (one song's lyrics came out garbled, and 《在遠方的你》 was transcribed as plain Chinese text), which is the known singing weakness.

name: 办公室小野 Ms Yeah
why: The regular office-cooking skits have short Mandarin dialogue (Sichuan-accented) over music. The 'en' clips all came from one atypical video, the 10-million-subscriber Diamond Play Button thank-you, which pulled the share down to 0.5.

name: BBC News 中文
why: The channel posts English-language BBC reports with Chinese subtitles (the US midterms piece and the Mbappé 'Asia Specific' segment hosted by Mariko Oi, both heard as English) alongside BBC Chinese's own Mandarin reports (the Taipei Pride video). With only 3 videos sampled, 25% isn't reliable; neither 'mostly Mandarin' (classifier, from memory) nor 'little Mandarin' fits. Low confidence.

name: Dianxi Xiaoge
why: 7 of 9 clips had no speech; the channel is long (25-150 min) cooking videos with ambient sound and a few lines of Yunnan dialect. The classifier itself says there is little talking, yet labels the channel 85% Mandarin, which would credit hours of mostly silent cooking as Mandarin listening.

name: YuYu love vlog
why: All 9 clips are Korean, including the China trip video where the Chinese girlfriend speaks Korean on camera; YouTube's auto-caption source language is ko. The classifier guessed 'mixed' from the couple's nationalities without evidence of the spoken language.

name: 日本電視台(Nippon TV)-NTV中文
why: Story narration is voiced over in Mandarin (the temple-stay piece, Matsui intro), while interviews, press conferences and 'full footage' videos stay in the original Japanese or German (the Takaichi–Merz video). Roughly half of the audio is Mandarin, as the audio found; the classifier couldn't tell.
